symptom: `CREATE OR MODIFY PERSISTENT ENTITY` on a Studio Pro-authored entity with an index was refused at exec: `1 element(s) kept their $ID but would be written with a different GUID — … (DomainModels$EntityIndex): stored X, would write <$ID>`. Attributes of the same entity were carried fine; `check -p` passed.
cause: `carryIndexIdentity` fell back to position only when the semantic index ID was EMPTY. The executor (`buildEntityFromStmt`) mints a FRESH ID for every declared index, so the ID was present and simply missed `storedByID`; the positional branch was never reached, the codec encoded `GUID = $ID`, `TransplantIDs` reattached the stored `$ID`, and `canon.StorageGUIDError` refused. Attributes survived only because their fallback pass is by name and runs for any unpaired attribute, not just ID-less ones.
insight: The #1119 carry tests modelled the statement-declared shape as 'members with no ID' and blanked the IDs themselves; the executor never does that, it mints fresh ones. A test of a write path must build its input the way the real caller does (here: fresh attribute, index and segment IDs, segments pointing at the fresh attribute IDs) — 'empty' and 'fresh-but-unknown' take different branches. Fallback passes must run on 'unpaired', not on 'has no key'. Second lesson: the index fallback must be POSITION, not the column list, even though the column list looks like the better identity — `TransplantIDs` aligns a nameless index list by position, so a GUID carried by columns onto a reordered list lands under its neighbour's `$ID` and the guard refuses it (tried, measured, reverted). The carry has to agree with the transplant's pairing or the guard turns the disagreement into a refusal. Proof: old binary refuses the pedapp repro (index GUID byte-patched away from $ID), fixed binary writes it with the GUID intact; reverting the fallback condition fails both new backend tests with the reported message.
